Encinitas, California 92024

1.

2.
ROLL CALL
3.
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE
4.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS / POSSIBLE DIRECTION TO STAFF (30 MINUTES)
Each speaker is allowed three (3) minutes to address the Planning Commission. All Oral Communications speaker requests must be received by the Clerk by the start of oral
communications. Up to 30 minutes are available for comments on items not on the agenda. Remarks must be addressed to the Planning Commission as a whole. State law prohibits Planning Commission action on non?agenda items. As appropriate, comments may be referred to the City Manager for follow?up or placement on a future agenda. Please be aware that the Mayor has the authority to reduce equally each speaker’s time to accommodate a larger number of speakers.
5.
CHANGES TO THE AGENDA Announcements of administrative changes to the agenda, in compliance with the Brown Act (open meetings for local bodies, California Government Code Section 54950 et seq.).
6.
CONSENT CALENDAR The recommendations on the following Consent Calendar will be enacted in one motion unless an item is removed from the Calendar. Any member of the public may remove an item by submitting a speaker request to the City Clerk. Each speaker is allowed three (3) minutes to address the Planning Commission. Please be aware that the Chair has the authority to reduce equally each speaker’s time to accommodate a larger number of speakers. Items removed from the Consent Calendar by a Planning Commissioner or the public will be considered immediately following the Consent Calendar.
6A.
APPROVAL OF MINUTES of the September 3, 2026, Planning Commission meeting.
STAFF CONTACT: Deana Gay, Planning Commission Clerk
Staff recommends approval.
Approval of the September 3, 2026 Minutes
6B.
PROJECT NAME: Shahri Addition and Remodel; CASE NUMBER: CDP-006339-2023; FILING DATE: June 26, 2023; APPLICANT: Tony and Stacy Shahri; LOCATION: 1500 Neptune Avenue (APN: 254-040-35-00); PROJECT DESCRIPTION: A coastal development permit to allow an addition and remodel of an existing single-family residence, inclusive of the addition of an attached one-car garage and an existing studio unit to be relocated and permitted as a junior accessory dwelling unit (JADU); ZONING/OVERLAY: Residential 11 (R-11), Coastal Bluff Overlay, Special Study Overlay, and the appeal jurisdiction of the California Coastal Commission within the Coastal Overlay Zone; ENVIRONMENTAL STATUS: The project has been determined to be exempt from environmental review pursuant to California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines Section 15301(e)(1), which exempts additions to existing structures provided that the addition is no more than 50 percent of the floor area of the structures before the addition, or 2,500 square feet. The proposed renovations and additions to the existing dwelling meet these criteria. None of the exceptions in Section 15300.2 of the CEQA Guidelines exist and no historical resources will be impacted by the proposed development.
STAFF CONTACT: Kaipo Eager-Kaninau, Associate Planner, (760) 633-2717 or kkaninau@encinitasca.gov.
Staff recommends approval

8A.
PROJECT NAME: Vulcan Avenue Pedestrian Path; CASE NUMBER: MULTI-008481-2025; DR-008530-2025; CDP-008529-2025; FILING DATE: 11/3/2025; APPLICANT: City of Encinitas; LOCATION: NCTD Right of Way, west of Vulcan avenue between La Costa Avenue and Leucadia Boulevard (APNs: 216-042-11; 254-323-01; 254-255-02; 254-255-01; 254-052-14; 254-060-16); PROJECT DESCRIPTION: A design review permit and coastal development permit for the construction of a pedestrian path and related improvements along the west side of Vulcan Avenue between La Costa Avenue and Leucadia Boulevard; ZONING/OVERLAY: North 101 Corridor Specific Plan, Transportation Corridor, Coastal Appeal Zone, Coastal Zone Sensitive Resource area, Cultural Natural Resources, Hillside Inland Bluff, Scenic Visual Corridor, Special Study, Coastal Zone Overlays; ENVIRONMENTAL STATUS: Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines, Section 15304 (a) – Class 4 - (Minor alterations to land) exempts minor public or private alterations in the condition of land, water, and/or vegetation which do not involve removal of healthy, mature, scenic trees. The project is consistent with this exemption, as it proposes the construction of a pedestrian path and minor grading. The project does not qualify as one of the exceptions prescribed under Section 15300.2 of the CEQA Guidelines and no historic resources are affected by the proposed project.
STAFF CONTACT: Fran Carr, Senior Planner, (760) 633-2738 or fcarr@encinitasca.gov.
Staff recommends approval
Vulcan Avenue Pedestrian Path - Report
Additional Correspondence 1
Additional Correspondence 2
8B.
CASE NUMBER: PLCY-008765-2026; APPLICANT: City of Encinitas; LOCATION: Citywide; PROJECT DESCRIPTION: Public hearing to consider an Ordinance to amend Title 30 (Zoning) of the Encinitas Municipal Code and amend the Local Coastal Program for the omnibus code clean up. ENVIRONMENTAL STATUS: The action before the Planning Commission is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) under Section 15061(b)(3) of the CEQA Guidelines because it can be seen with certainty that there is no possibility that the activity in question may have a significant effect on the environment. The action is also exempt from CEQA under Section 15378(b)(5) of the CEQA Guidelines because it involves an organizational or administrative activity of government that will not result in the direct or indirect physical change in the environment.
STAFF CONTACT: Charlotte Brenner, Associate Planner: (760) 633-2784 or cbrenner@encinitasca.gov.
Staff recommends the Planning Commission adopt PC Resolution No. 2026-30 and make recommendations to City Council recommending the approval and adoption of Ordinance No. 2026-14.
